How the game works

Every player is classified.
Every team is balanced.

Each player is rated from 1.0 to 5.0 depending on trunk control and function — 1.0 for the most impairment, 5.0 for the least. A 5.0 can be an able-bodied player: they play too. It's not a ranking of skill. It's what makes the line-up fair.

  • In British domestic league play, the five players a team fields can never total more than 14 points combined
  • A low-point player and a high-point player are equally valuable on court
  • It's the rule that lets a first-season player and a national-squad player share a line-up

Fixtures & results

Every Jaguars squad plays in a league run by British Wheelchair Basketball — the national governing body sets the calendar, and results feed straight into the official standings.

British Wheelchair Basketball

Premiership · National League · Development calendars

Fixtures, results and league tables are hosted on the BWB competitions hub, not on this site — so you're always looking at the official, up-to-date source.

Get involved

Training is open to anyone

You don't need a sport chair, a diagnosis, or any experience to come and try it. We provide chairs, qualified coaches run every session, and the only stupid question is the one you didn't ask.

Beginners

First session

Come along, borrow a chair, learn the basics of pushing, pivoting and passing. No commitment, no pressure.

Junior

Youth sessions

A dedicated space for younger players to build skills and confidence alongside the senior squads.

Performance

Squad training

Structured, competitive sessions for players training toward league selection.

We train and play at Bowbridge Rd, Newark-on-Trent, Newark NG24 4BZ, 19:30–22:00.

Membership

Come and play

Whoever you are, whatever your skill level or ability — young players, experienced players, first-timers and internationals all train together. You don't need your own chair to start.
